events.title: Quirq'y Workshop: Building & Running AI Agents
events.description:
Coffee & Code Philly
# Quirqây Workshop: Building & Running AI Agents

Join Coffee&Code Philadelphia and **Quirq** for a hands-on online workshop designed to help you build, run, and understand an AI agent working with real data.
This is a practical build sessionânot just a presentation. By the end of the workshop, youâll have launched an agent inside a managed workspace, connected it to your own data, assigned it a real task, and observed what it did while running.
The workshop will be led by **Suraj Sharma, Founder of Quirq**.

## What youâll learn

* How to launch a cloud-managed AI agent using [app.xo.builders](https://app.xo.builders/)
* How to connect a repository, folder of documents, spreadsheet, or other work data
* How to assign your agent a real task
* How to inspect its environment, activity, file changes, sessions, and costs
* How to switch between agent runtimes while keeping the same workspace
* How to run the same open-source workspace locally
* How to contribute to **xo-space** through GitHub Discussions and pull requests
* How to participate in the Quirq challenges at the Coffee&Code Philadelphia AI Agent Hackathon

Supported quickstarts include Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, N8N, and bring-your-own runtime options.

## Who should attend?

This workshop is for developers who are registeredâor considering registeringâfor the **Coffee&Code Philadelphia AI Agent Hackathon on September 20**.
No previous agent-building experience is required. Whether you already work with coding agents or are launching one for the first time, youâll leave with a working environment and a clear path toward a hackathon project.

## Before the workshop

Please come prepared with:

* An account at [app.xo.builders](https://app.xo.builders/)
* A model API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, or another supported provider
* Some data you are comfortable giving your agent access to, such as a code repository, document folder, or spreadsheet
* Access to the Coffee&Code Philadelphia Discord

Model API credits are not provided, so participants should bring their own API key.
Prefer to work locally? You can install xo-space without creating an account:
`curl -fsSL quirq.ai/install | sh`

## Workshop schedule

**6:00â6:15 PM â Welcome and introduction**
Meet Quirq, learn about the hackathon track, and explore why agents benefit from persistent, observable workspaces.
**6:15â7:00 PM â Live agent build**
Follow along as we launch a workspace, import real data, assign an agent a task, inspect its activity, and switch between supported runtimes.
**7:00â7:25 PM â Contributing to xo-space**
Explore the open-source repository and its GitHub Discussions. Learn how to select a contribution idea, claim a thread, submit a pull request, and build a strong hackathon contribution.
**7:25â7:40 PM â Quirq hackathon challenges**
Review the Build It challenge, Red Team bounty, judging criteria, eligible projects, and submission requirements.
**7:40â8:00 PM â Q&A and setup support**
Get help launching your environment and resolving any remaining setup issues.

## Continue at the AI Agent Hackathon

Participants can use what they build during this workshop as the starting point for a project at the **Coffee&Code Philadelphia AI Agent Hackathon** on Sunday, September 20, at Pennovation Works.
The Quirq track includes:

* **Build It:** $500 cash plus equivalent Quirq credits for the strongest agentic system built and demonstrated using Quirq
* **Red Team Bounty:** A points-based bounty pool of up to $500 for validated security findings against a participantâs own cloud-managed workspace

Quirq engineers will also provide support through the dedicated `#quirq-track` channel in the Coffee&Code Philadelphia Discord before and throughout the hackathon.
Come with an API key and some real data. Leave with an agent already runningâand an idea you can take directly into the hackathon.

events.title: Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses
events.description:
Coffee & Code Philly
## Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses

This is a casual pair-programming meetup for developers experimenting with Claude Code, Codex, and agentic coding workflows.
There is no formal presentation and no fixed curriculum. Bring a laptop, a repository, a side project, or a workflow you want to test. We will work in small groups, compare approaches, debug problems, and share what is working.

Possible areas to explore include:

* Building iterative coding-agent loops
* Comparing Claude Code and Codex on the same task
* Designing graph-based agent workflows
* Creating reusable coding harnesses
* Managing context across large repositories
* Running tests and validating agent-generated changes
* Using sandboxes, permissions, and approval steps
* Coordinating subagents or parallel tasks
* Measuring latency, token usage, cost, and completion quality
* Debugging failed or incomplete agent runs

You do not need to be an expert in either tool. This meetup is for people who want hands-on time to experiment, pair with other developers, and learn through building.
Bring something you are working on, or join someone elseâs project.
Hosted by **Coffee & Code Philadelphia**.
